dedupe_keys.name: organisation and operation of the suwaseriya 1990 pre hospital ambulance service sri lanka

description: This case study describes how Sri Lanka built a free national ambulance service, Suwaseriya 1990, and how it runs. The producers of the review are Indika Wanninayake and Hemantha Ranasinghe, public health officials in Sri Lanka's Ministry of Health, who published a desk review in 2022 based on the World Health Organization health system framework. Coverage: the service started in two provinces in July 2016 and has covered the whole island since July 2018 under a foundation set up by an act of parliament. It operates 297 ambulances based at police stations, dispatched by a 24-hour command and control centre whose 40-seat call centre handles about 5,300 calls a day; doctors in the centre advise the emergency medical technicians at the scene and choose the receiving hospital, and GPS tracking linked to live traffic picks the fastest, not the nearest ambulance. The article is available as a free PDF from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: a descriptive review in a minor journal, response times are stated inconsistently as minutes and seconds, and no call-level data are published. Simulation uses: parameters for national ambulance system models, such as fleet size, station placement at police posts and call volumes. Related records: the ambulance deployment data for Fez-Meknes (data-fez-meknes-ambulance-deployment) and OpenEMS (model-openems-ambulance-deployment) support such modelling.
name: Organisation and operation of the Suwaseriya 1990 pre-hospital ambulance service, Sri Lanka
outcomes: The desk review reports island-wide free pre-hospital care since July 2018, with 98.9% of calls answered on the first ring and average response times reported as 8.38 in Colombo and 14.32 elsewhere (units given inconsistently as minutes and seconds in the article). Gaps include no triage or standardised times, no external quality monitoring and missing policies on equity, quality and risk reduction.
